concepts.def: Worldview shaping how individuals/societies evaluate environmental issues; ecocentric, anthropocentric, technocentric (IBDP categorisation).
Meeting present needs without compromising ability of future generations to meet theirs (Brundtland 1987).
Individual rational use of shared resource leads to collective ruin (Hardin 1968 in Science).
1992 Rio Conference produced Agenda 21, UNFCCC and CBD; landmark in environmental governance.
Where serious damage threatens, lack of full scientific certainty should not delay preventive action.
Analysing environment as interlinked open systems with inputs, outputs, flows, feedbacks.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Environmental Law — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Environmental Law brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Environmental Law.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
